pages.text: "So warm! My place!" Bami sat close to the dining-car stove, in the very middle of its circle of light. Outside, snowy mountains were white.
Pipi called a station. Three sheep sisters in matching hats boarded with little bags. "Cold! A stove!" cried the youngest. Bami fluffed their feathers to block more of the circle. "I'm not warm yet!"
The sisters stood shivering outside the circle. The youngest sniffled. "We want some warmth, too..." Bami shut their eyes and pretended not to hear.
Nabi rolled from the window into one side of the circle, belly up and purring in the firelight. Bami opened their eyes. "Taking my place, too?"
Soon Nabi rolled back out and lay by the window with a warm tummy, purring again. Bami blinked. "Nabi moves aside after getting warm!"
Bami touched their chest with their beak. Already warm! They stepped aside. "Take turns by the stove! Eldest sister next!"
The eldest warmed her feet in the circle. "Much better!" Bami and the other two waited in line. Bami wanted to stamp impatiently but held still. Take turns by the stove!
At last, the youngest had her turn. She smiled inside the circle. The dining car was warm, and all three sisters' wool fluffed softly. Bami spread their wings. "Waiting made us all warm!"
Next day, Bami moved aside first and counted. "One, get warm, then move over! Two, wait for my next turn! Three, after everyone, it's my turn again!" Nabi waved a tail by the window.
The eldest hugged Bami in her soft wool. "Thanks to you, all three of us are warm." Taking turns in the circle warmed everyone. Take turns by the stove! Snowy mountains sparkled outside.
